case_title: Shri Satish Kumar & Anr. v. State of Himachal Pradesh & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour (one accused's house was in front of the victim's daughter's house); prior land dispute with one accused, alleged by the prosecution and not proved
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; Arms Act s.25; Arms Act s.27
weapon: Single barrel gun (licensed to one accused's father) with empty and live cartridges
evidence_type: Circumstantial; recovery on disclosure statements; forensic science report; post-mortem; telephone call; testimony of hostile witnesses
confession: Disclosure statements of two accused (linked to recovery of body and gun); not relied on because the recovery in pursuance of them was not proved
high_court_outcome: Complainant's appeal allowed; acquittal set aside; all accused convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC and Arms Act ss.25 and 27
neutral_facts: The victim left home in the morning, saying he would visit a relative in a nearby village and then report for duty. He did not return by evening, and his mobile phone was switched off. The next morning the victim's daughter was told by a forest guard that he had not reported for duty. She then telephoned a person who lived opposite her house and asked for a contact number at the village. At about 7:15 am on the following day, the police received a telephone call from one of the accused reporting that the victim had died of a gunshot. A police team went towards the place of occurrence. Later that day the victim's daughter gave a statement naming two accused as the shooters, saying she had learned this from police when they came to the village. The police took the two accused, two local witnesses and the daughter to a forest about two kilometres from the house. There the victim's body was found, along with a bag and two pellet marks on nearby bushes. Both accused were said to have made disclosure statements in the presence of the two witnesses, leading to the body and a single-barrel gun with cartridges being recovered; the gun was licensed to a third person and was found at his house. Forensic examination reported that a cartridge had been fired from the gun and that gunshot residue on the victim's clothes indicated distant firing. The post-mortem found multiple perforated gunshot wounds and recorded death from cardio-respiratory failure and hypovolemic shock due to gunshot injury. Both witnesses to the disclosure statements later denied in cross-examination that any such statement was made in their presence. The investigating officer's accounts of when the death became known were said to be contradictory, and no call records were produced to verify the telephone call. The alleged motive was a land dispute with one of the accused.
physical_harm: Death from multiple gunshot wounds (perforated wounds to body; cardio-respiratory failure and hypovolemic shock)
motive: alleged: land dispute with one accused (Satish Kumar); the court held the prosecution failed to prove any motive and the alleged motive had no foundation
key_evidence_accepted: None relied on for conviction. The court noted only that the forensic report showed the gun was used in the crime, which did not establish which accused fired
witness_credibility: Witnesses to disclosure statements (PW-2, PW-3) turned hostile and were not trustworthy; investigating officer's statements were contradictory; the daughter's first statement recorded at 12.45 pm naming the assailants was doubtful; evidence did not inspire confidence
post_offence_conduct: One accused allegedly telephoned police at 7:15 am reporting the death; disclosure statements and recoveries allegedly followed, but the court found the telephone call unverified and the recoveries not proved
custody_duration: Not stated (arrest on 22 December 2009 noted; duration of custody not given)
bail_history: Not stated (bail bonds were furnished; no grant or refusal details given)
trial_duration: offence: 21 December 2009 (deceased left home; death reported 22 December 2009); trial judgment: 30 November 2012; High Court: 20 September 2016; Supreme Court: 2 March 2020
legal_representation: Accused: Ruchi Kohli, Babita Yadav, Amit Sharma, Srishti Mishra, R. C. Kohli (Advocates). State: Upasana Nath, Abhinav Mukerji, Radhika Gautam (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR No. 218 registered 22 December 2009; post-mortem, forensic examination and recoveries carried out; trial completed with acquittal
procedural_irregularity: Investigating officer gave contradictory statements; police did not verify the telephone call; the FIR's account of cause of death suggested the body was known before recovery; disclosure-based recovery not proved
appeal_history: Trial court: all accused acquitted (30 November 2012). High Court: complainant's appeal allowed, acquittal set aside, accused convicted (20 September 2016). Supreme Court: appeals allowed, convictions set aside, acquittal restored (2 March 2020)
prosecution_argument: Not stated (State's submissions before the Supreme Court are not recorded; the judgment records the High Court's reasoning that post-mortem and forensic reports showed use of the gun and that recoveries corroborated the disclosure statements)
defence_argument: Case rested wholly on circumstantial evidence not meeting the required chain; prosecution witnesses gave contradictory statements, so the truthfulness of the prosecution case was doubtful
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain consistent only with guilt; an appellate court may interfere with acquittal only if the trial court's findings are perverse or not possible on the evidence
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; Brajendra Singh v. State of M.P. (2012) 4 SCC 289; Chandrappa and Others v. State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds discharged; all accused to be set at liberty if not wanted in any other case

number_of_accused.quote: Criminal Appeal No. 19 of 2017 is preferred by Satish Kumar and Rajeev Kumar whereas Criminal Appeal No 1109 of 2016 is preferred by Lekh Ram

victim_gender.quote: Neelam Sharma had stated that her father left home at about 8 am on 21st December, 2009

accused_victim_relationship.quote: The motive of murder was said to be land dispute with Satish Kumar pending in Shimla High Court.

offence_category.quote: the Appellants were convicted for the offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860

statutory_provisions.quote: convicted for the offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 1 as well as under Sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act, 1959

weapon.quote: The other incriminating circumstance weighed with the High Court is the recovery of the single barrel gun with the cartridge from the house of Lekh Ram, the licence holder.

evidence_type.quote: In a case based upon circumstantial evidence motive is relevant

confession.quote: the recovery of dead body in pursuance of similar disclosure statements made by accused Satish Kumar and Rajeev Kumar is not proved

trial_court_outcome.quote: the learned trial court acquitted all the accused for the reason that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

high_court_outcome.quote: whereby the appeal filed by the complainant was allowed and the order of acquittal passed by the learned trial court on 30th November, 2012 was set aside

final_outcome.quote: The order of acquittal recorded by the trial court is restored.

number_of_offences.quote: The conviction of the appellants for the offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC and Sections 25 and 27 of the Act is set aside.
